about.title: About IPFlex: Enterprise Proxy Services, Delivery Method, and Support Principles
about.description: Learn what IPFlex does, how the team delivers proxy services, what support principles it follows, and how data governance is handled for evaluation, PoC, and production rollout.

header.title: About IPFlex
header.description: This page gives procurement, technical, and operations teams a clear view of what IPFlex does, where it fits, and how proxy delivery is handled before they move into product pages or documentation.

whatWeDo.title: What IPFlex Does
whatWeDo.description: IPFlex provides enterprise proxy capability across static residential, dynamic residential, and datacenter proxy services. The focus is not only on node access, but on making proxy capacity usable in a defined workload, onboarding path, and stability model.
facts: Covers three core proxy capabilities: static residential, dynamic residential, and datacenter proxies.
Provides layered support through a help center, onboarding docs, a resource hub, and playbooks.
Supports use cases such as data collection, ad verification, cross-border e-commerce, account stability, and geo-visibility validation.
Helps teams make consistent decisions across evaluation, PoC, onboarding, and scale-up phases.

evaluation.title: How to Evaluate Fit
evaluation.description: Proxy capability should be evaluated when teams face session stability, account consistency, geo-visibility validation, high-volume collection, or predictable budget requirements. Fit depends on session requirements, coverage targets, throughput boundaries, and acceptable cost.
questions: Does the workflow require long sessions or a stable identity?
Does it require geo-level coverage or exit rotation?
Is high-throughput capacity a primary goal?
Can the evaluation be measured with success ratio, latency, and unit cost?

items.title: Define the workload before choosing the proxy type
items.description: The selection process starts with session stability, coverage, throughput, and cost boundaries, then maps the workload to static residential, dynamic residential, or datacenter proxies.

items.title: Use measurable metrics for PoC and scale-up
items.description: Evaluation should prioritize success ratio, P95 latency, recovery time after blocks, challenge trigger rate, and cost per completed workflow instead of subjective impressions.

items.title: Extend delivery into onboarding and operations
items.description: The team treats proxy delivery as an operational capability that includes authentication, access control, logging, troubleshooting, and routine optimization.

proxyGuide.description: Compare static residential, dynamic residential, and datacenter proxy fit first.

resources.title: Resources
resources.description: Open definitions, onboarding docs, use cases, and selected execution playbooks.

items.q: What teams is IPFlex best suited for?
items.a: It is best suited for teams that need stable proxy capability as part of a repeatable operating workflow, including data collection, e-commerce operations, ad verification, risk control, and geo-validation.

items.q: How is this page different from product pages and the help center?
items.a: The About page explains positioning, delivery method, and governance principles. Product pages explain workload fit. The help center covers API, authentication, and operational instructions.

items.q: What should teams confirm before procurement or onboarding?
items.a: Teams should first confirm whether the workload needs session stability, exit rotation, or high-throughput capacity, then validate success ratio, latency, recovery, and unit cost before rollout.
